title: Nanoscale Characterization of Zirconium Alloy Corrosion: Dissolved Oxygen-Induced Microstructural Transformations
content: Different nuclear reactor types exhibit dramatically varying dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations, ranging from less than 10 parts per billion to several parts per million [1]. These substantial variations in oxygen environment fundamentally alter the microstructure and corrosion characteristics of zirconium-based fuel cladding materials [2].
